title: TypeScript & the build loop
summary: Catch mistakes before your browser runs the code.
points: TypeScript checks JavaScript with type information. It does not replace JavaScript’s runtime behavior.
A .ts source file normally needs a build step for browsers. Type annotations disappear from emitted JavaScript.
Use a project tsconfig.json with strict checking. Run tsc --noEmit for a check without generating files.
The starter uses Vite to serve and bundle code, and a separate type-check command. A successful bundle alone is not proof that types passed.
Read the first diagnostic, fix its cause, and rerun the check. Avoid turning checks off just to make errors disappear.
mistake: A type annotation does not add a runtime validation check.
challenge: Change minutes to a string and inspect the compiler error. Restore it and run the starter build.

diagram.caption: Catch mistakes before your browser runs the code.

title: Inference & everyday types
summary: Let values suggest types; describe boundaries explicitly.
points: Inference gives let count = 0 the type number. An annotation is useful at an API or ambiguous empty value.
Use lowercase string, number, and boolean for ordinary values. An array of titles can be string[].
A literal union such as "all"
"active" limits the allowed strings. It is more specific than string.
any disables many checks and spreads through code. unknown requires narrowing before use.
strictNullChecks keeps null and undefined distinct. Check a possibly missing value before using it.

rows: Derive a type from a value
A small set of allowed values

mistake: An assertion such as value as number does not convert a string to a number.
challenge: Type a view selector with all, active, and completed. Try an invalid spelling and inspect the diagnostic.

diagram.title: Inference & everyday types
diagram.caption: Let values suggest types; describe boundaries explicitly.

title: Objects, interfaces & readonly
summary: Describe the shape of a task without freezing it by accident.
points: An interface or type alias describes object properties. Structural compatibility depends on the shape, not the name of the interface.
A property with ? may be absent; reading it can produce undefined. Handle the missing case.
readonly prevents assignment through that type during checking. It is not runtime Object.freeze.
An intersection A & B requires both sets of properties. A union A
B allows alternatives.
Copy an object with spread before updating it. A shallow copy does not recursively clone nested objects.
mistake: readonly is a compile-time restriction, not a storage or security boundary.
challenge: Add an optional due date to Task and render a fallback when it is missing.

diagram.title: Objects, interfaces & readonly
diagram.caption: Describe the shape of a task without freezing it by accident.

title: Typed functions & callbacks
summary: Make inputs, outputs, and side effects easy to understand.
points: Annotate parameters at function boundaries. Return types can be inferred, or written explicitly to document a contract.
A callback type describes the function passed into another function, for example (id: string) => void.
An optional parameter can be undefined. A default parameter supplies a value when the argument is missing or undefined.
void means callers should not rely on a return value. Promise<T> describes the eventual value of an asynchronous operation.
Do not mark a callback parameter optional unless the caller may actually omit it. Keep types aligned with the calling code.
mistake: A return annotation describes a contract; it does not convert an incorrect returned value.
challenge: Type a rename function and an onRemove callback. Check wrong argument types and missing required arguments.

diagram.title: Typed functions & callbacks
diagram.caption: Make inputs, outputs, and side effects easy to understand.

title: Unions & narrowing
summary: Check which case you have before using it.
points: A union permits several shapes; only operations valid for the current narrowed case are safe.
typeof checks narrow primitives. typeof null is object, so object checks must also exclude null.
A shared literal status can discriminate object variants such as loading, success, and error.
Optional chaining returns undefined for a nullish receiver. It does not prove that arbitrary data has the expected shape.
An exhaustive switch can assign the remaining value to never. Adding a new variant then reveals forgotten cases.
mistake: A truthiness check can accidentally exclude valid values such as 0 or an empty string.
challenge: Model idle, loading, success, and error as a union. Render a message for each case without non-null assertions.

diagram.title: Unions & narrowing
diagram.caption: Check which case you have before using it.

title: Generics & useful type tools
summary: Preserve relationships instead of erasing types.
points: A generic parameter relates input and output types. It is useful when the same operation works for several types.
A constraint such as T extends { id: string } states the minimum shape an operation needs.
keyof T describes the property keys of T. Indexed access T[K] describes a property’s value type.
Pick selects properties, Omit removes them, Partial makes them optional, and Readonly restricts typed writes.
Utility types change static descriptions only. They do not validate a request, remove runtime fields, or deep-freeze data.
mistake: An array can be empty. A generic return type should not promise an element that may not exist.
challenge: Write byId<T extends { id: string }> returning T | undefined. Test an existing and a missing ID.

diagram.title: Generics & useful type tools
diagram.caption: Preserve relationships instead of erasing types.

title: Typed DOM & form events
summary: Connect types to real elements and real user input.
points: DOM queries may return null. Check the result before reading element-specific properties.
An instanceof HTMLInputElement check verifies the runtime element kind and narrows its TypeScript type.
Input .value is a string; .checked is a boolean for checkboxes. Convert numeric text deliberately and validate it.
Listen to form submit to support Enter as well as button clicks. preventDefault stops the browser’s normal submission.
A type assertion or non-null assertion can silence a diagnostic without ensuring that an element exists. Prefer a runtime guard at this boundary.
output: With a #title input containing Read, logs Read. Without that input, the block is skipped.
mistake: querySelector<HTMLInputElement> supplies a static expectation; it does not verify the element kind at runtime.
challenge: Guard a title input and checkbox, then submit a form using only the keyboard.

diagram.title: Typed DOM & form events
diagram.caption: Connect types to real elements and real user input.

title: Unknown data & validation
summary: Validate at the boundary before trusting a typed value.
points: JSON.parse and network responses can contain unexpected shapes. Assign external data to unknown and check it.
Check arrays, non-null objects, required property types, bounds, and duplicate IDs before accepting task data.
A type predicate promises the compiler that its check is correct. An incomplete predicate creates false confidence.
Check response.ok for HTTP errors, then parse and validate JSON. Network success does not imply valid application data.
Catch failures explicitly and preserve unreadable saved data. A validation error should not silently replace it with an empty saved list.
mistake: Writing JSON.parse(raw) as Task[] does not validate even one task.
challenge: Write a task validator. Reject null, duplicate IDs, a string done flag, and a blank title while preserving the original stored text.

diagram.title: Unknown data & validation
diagram.caption: Validate at the boundary before trusting a typed value.

title: Modules & project checks
summary: Keep a small project understandable and reproducible.
points: Use export and import to split responsibilities into modules. Type-only imports describe contracts without importing runtime values.
Keep model logic separate from DOM wiring so it can be checked without a browser.
A browser needs JavaScript output. Vite can transform TypeScript while tsc --noEmit checks the whole project separately.
A package lock records dependency resolution. npm ci installs the locked project dependencies and fails when the manifest disagrees.
Run type checks, meaningful tests, and a production build. A green type check does not prove keyboard behavior, network availability, or business correctness.
mistake: A bundler successfully removing types is not the same as checking them.
challenge: Extract Task and pure transformations to model.ts. Import the type separately and run the locked build.

diagram.title: Modules & project checks
diagram.caption: Keep a small project understandable and reproducible.

title: Build a typed planner
summary: Use types to clarify a working browser project.
points: The starter ports the JavaScript planner to strict TypeScript, with a Task contract and a finite view union.
Validate stored and fetched data at runtime; keep compile-time contracts and runtime checks together.
Use stable task IDs, immutable transformations, safe text rendering, and a full saved array independent of the current filter.
Storage is local to a browser and origin. Read failures offer temporary mode without overwriting existing data; failed writes show feedback.
Extend the project with optional due dates and editing. Update validation and old-data handling before changing the persisted shape.
mistake: Types cannot stop another tab or a user from changing browser storage; validate every load.
challenge: Extend the downloadable starter, keep its checks passing, then test reload, corrupt storage, filters, and keyboard focus.

diagram.caption: Use types to clarify a working browser project.
